articles.title: How to Build a Browser-Based Jigsaw Puzzle Game with JavaScript and HTML5 Canvas
articles.excerpt: Building a jigsaw puzzle game for the browser is an interesting combination of geometry, graphics programming, and interactive game development. Unlike a traditional grid-based puzzle, a jigsaw puzzle…
articles.body: Building a jigsaw puzzle game for the browser is an interesting combination of geometry, graphics programming, and interactive game development. Unlike a traditional grid-based puzzle, a jigsaw puzzle requires irregular piece shapes, matching edges, image clipping, and precise drag-and-drop interactions. Players should be able to move individual pieces, connect matching pieces, and gradually reconstruct the original image. In this tutorial, we'll explore how to build a browser-based jigsaw puzzle game using JavaScript and HTML5 Canvas, starting with the basic game architecture and moving through piece generation, rendering, interaction, and performance optimization.

articles.title: AI Financial Reporting: A 14-Case Release Gate for Close Narratives
articles.excerpt: AI Financial Reporting: A 14-Case Release Gate for Close Narratives A finance team should treat an AI-written close narrative as a proposal, not as a number source or a self-approving control. The pra…
articles.body: AI Financial Reporting: A 14-Case Release Gate for Close Narratives A finance team should treat an AI-written close narrative as a proposal, not as a number source or a self-approving control. The practical sequence is: freeze the reporting period and data snapshot; reconcile every material figure to an owned source; draft explanations with claims linked to those figures; run deterministic checks; obtain a named preparer and independent reviewer; then release a versioned report with its evidence and approval record. If the source data, accounting mapping, period, or approval is uncertain, the safe output is a hold with a precise reason. This guide turns that rule into a reusable release protocol and a small executable gate.

articles.title: Demystifying the MCP Protocol for Open Source AI
articles.excerpt: The MCP protocol is the connective tissue for many open source AI workflows—yet is often treated as a black box. Here’s a developer’s-eye primer on why MCP matters, how it relates to A2A and CLI adapt…
articles.body: The MCP protocol is the connective tissue for many open source AI workflows—yet is often treated as a black box. Here’s a developer’s-eye primer on why MCP matters, how it relates to A2A and CLI adapters, and where runtimes like apcore step up to fill governance, audit, and multi-protocol gaps. MCP defines how an agent or model can discover, describe, and invoke remote tools. Classic “bare server” MCP implementations give you a surface, but they don’t enforce validation or traceability. Projects aiming for responsible agent development are increasingly layering governed runtimes that check schemas, approvals, and usage evidence before anything is exposed to MCP or A2A.

articles.body: Mira Murati's lab just shipped its second model. It's a big one. And the part everyone actually wants — the downloadable weights — isn't here yet. Thinking Machines Lab announced Inkling 2 Small on 5 November 2026: a 594-billion-parameter sparse mixture-of-experts model aimed at long-horizon autonomous work, coding, vision and knowledge tasks. It scores 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 18 points above the first generation's Inkling Small. Artificial Analysis says that once the weights are released, it would be the highest-scoring open-weights model developed outside China. Read that sentence again, because the word doing all the work is "once". At launch, Inkling 2 Small is closed weights. You can use it through Thinking Machines' Tinker platform and its Playground.

This weekly issue is written only from that ledger and the files beside it, so nothing in it can be backfilled later. Week: Friday 30 October to Thursday 5 November 2026. 1. I'm not going to invent a reason. 2. The number that changed a decision: 7 → 515 One of the sites, MonitoringRoom, has a page on the US midterms that shows what prediction markets priced. articles.title: Agent Skill for Debugging Things
articles.excerpt: Today, I want to create an agent skill for debugging. Sometimes, I receive bug reports or tickets from QA, but I don't always know where to start the investigation or what prompts to use. I decided to…
articles.body: Today, I want to create an agent skill for debugging. Sometimes, I receive bug reports or tickets from QA, but I don't always know where to start the investigation or what prompts to use. I decided to use the Engineering: Debug skill to help with this process. However, its responses can sometimes be too long, with large paragraphs that are difficult to follow. I want to improve the skill so that it breaks the investigation into clear, structured sections, such as Root Cause , How the Issue Occurs , and other relevant topics. This will make the investigation easier to understand, review, and share with the development team. That's why I decided to create Panda Debugger , an agent skill designed to make debugging investigations more structured, clear, and easier to follow.

articles.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
articles.excerpt: Certain configurations of Alpine are affected. Other distros may be as well.
articles.body: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations.

articles.body: Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT).

articles.title: Blue Origin announces 3rd stage for its powerful New Glenn rocket —and a new engine
articles.excerpt: Blue Origin has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the launcher even more flexible and capable. The company has also built a new engine, called Northstar.
articles.body: Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . "The third stage enables direct deployment of satellite constellations to GEO [ geostationary orbit ] and supports heavy-lift science and exploration missions to the moon and deep space." Illustration of the variants of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, with the new GS3 third stage now in the mix. (Image credit: Blue Origin) New Glenn is a two-stage vehicle at the moment.

articles.title: Earth has captured a new mini moon  — but it won't stick around for long
articles.excerpt: Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and QQ8 is sticking around for Christmas.
articles.body: Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and it is sticking around for Christmas. The space rock, designated 2026 QQ8, was first observed in August 2026 after entering orbit around Earth in April 2026. The discovery was reported by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center on Thursday (Oct. 29). The stay of QQ8 is a temporary one. The mini-moon will remain in the thrall of Earth's gravity through December before breaking away in 2027. Scientists have recreated the orbital path of QQ8, finding that it takes 359 days, or about 0.98 of an Earth year, to orbit the sun . QQ8 closely approaches Earth around once every ten years, but this time the object came so close that Earth has been able to gravitationally seize it.
